name: GoHighLevel
verdict: Self-serve: a Private app needs no review but is unlisted, and whether unrelated customers can install it at scale is unconfirmed. Public Marketplace listing needs review and a demo video.
needGuide: Yes — choose the app type and install scope (sub-account or agency) carefully, then decide whether to list.

auth.detail: Authorization-code grant for v2 APIs; token endpoint https://services.leadconnectorhq.com/oauth/token with user_type Company (agency tokens) or Location (sub-account tokens). Access tokens last about 24 hours; refresh tokens last 1 year if unused and rotate on each use. An agency token can mint location tokens via /oauth/locationToken. PKCE not documented.

effort.timeToProduction: unknown; private install likely days, public listing review time not published

approval.gate: Private apps need no review but are not listed. Public Marketplace listing requires review against the App Review Guidelines (HTTPS redirect on a verified domain, minimal scopes, working install, support channel with 24-hour first response, uninstall/disconnect flow, and a Loom demo video as the final submission step). Whether private apps can be installed by unrelated customers at scale was not confirmed.

scopes.why: Scopes are selected per app and reviewers ask you to justify them.
scopes.summary: Scopes are selected per app in Advanced Settings -> Auth (for example contacts, conversations, workflows, locations); request only what you need because reviewers ask you to justify them. The exact scope list is in the Scopes docs (not read).

cost: Free developer account (likely); customers need their own HighLevel subscription
prerequisites: Account and owner: A developer with a HighLevel Developer Account (sign in at marketplace.gohighlevel.com); use a company-owned login. Whether a paid agency plan is required was not stated.
Where you register: Developer Marketplace -> My Apps -> Create App; Advanced Settings -> Auth (scopes, redirect URL, Installation URL); Manage -> Secrets -> Client Keys -> Add
Cost: Free developer account (likely); customers need their own HighLevel subscription

registerAt.path: Developer Marketplace -> My Apps -> Create App; Advanced Settings -> Auth (scopes, redirect URL, Installation URL); Manage -> Secrets -> Client Keys -> Add

steps.do: Sign in to marketplace.gohighlevel.com -> My Apps -> Create App; set App Type Private, Target User Sub-account, Who Can Install, Listing Type
Advanced Settings -> Auth: pick minimum scopes, add HTTPS redirect URL, copy the Installation URL
Manage -> Secrets -> Client Keys -> Add; store client ID and secret (secret shown once)
Create a Sandbox account and install the app; exchange code at /oauth/token with the right user_type; refresh and persist rotated refresh tokens
For agency installs, call /oauth/locationToken per sub-account and handle uninstall events
Complete Profile (logo, category, description, screenshots), record a Loom demo of install, setup, core flow, errors and disconnect
Switch to Public and submit for review; set up support email or phone

roles.team: A developer with a HighLevel Developer Account (sign in at marketplace.gohighlevel.com); use a company-owned login. Whether a paid agency plan is required was not stated.
roles.console: none documented in the pages read.
roles.customer: A sub-account (location) admin installs for one location; an agency admin installs at agency level or in bulk, which yields Company-type tokens. Target User and Who Can Install settings decide who sees the app.

testing: Create a Sandbox (App Test) account and a Private Integration Token for it, install the app through the private install link, and verify OAuth, scopes, API behavior and webhooks; a pre-release checklist is in the App Testing Guide.

blockers.problem: Using the wrong user_type returns the wrong token level
blockers.fix: Company tokens cannot make location calls without exchanging for a location token.
Failing to save the new one breaks the connection until reinstall.

blockers.problem: Whitelabel apps must not show HighLevel or GHL branding anywhere, including OAuth screens
Redirect URLs must be HTTPS and match a verified domain or review fails

automation.agentCan: Write the OAuth and location-token code, set up webhook handlers, draft listing copy, scope justifications and the Loom script, run sandbox test calls.
automation.humanMust: Developer account sign-in, install into the sandbox, record the Loom demo, submit for review, provide support contact.

uncertain: Public review timeline, private-app install limits for external customers, and whether an agency plan is needed to host a developer account were not documented on the pages read.
